limitations_and_boundaries: The study does not include a rescue experiment for the classical complement cascade (C1q) to confirm its lack of involvement.
The protective effects of AAV-Crry were specific to the retinogeniculate circuit and not observed in the somatosensory cortex.
The study does not assess long-term functional outcomes beyond peak disease.

missed_core_items.description: The study used both male and female mice, but the main analyses were performed in males; females showed similar but less robust synapse loss.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: the bulk of our analyses in male mice. Also, in humans, while males are less prone to MS compared to females, they tend to develop more aggressive forms of the disease with more disability

missed_core_items.description: Synapse loss in EAE was observed in both male and female mice, but effects were less robust in females.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Note that in EAE, similar synapse loss was observed in female mice (Figures S4A and S4C). However, these effects were less robust compared to male mice

missed_core_items.description: The study assessed synapse loss at both onset and peak of EAE; at peak, mild demyelination, neuron loss, and axon degeneration became apparent, but AAV-Crry still protected synapses.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: To assess long-term effects of AAV-Crry, we also assessed synapses at peak disease ± AAV-Crry in a separate cohort of EAE mice (Figure S6A). First, in control AAV-EGFP mice, synapse loss was still observed, and mild but significant demyelination, neuron loss, and axon degeneration became apparent in the retinogeniculate circuit at peak EAE (Figures S6B–S6D). However, in AAV-Crry mice, synapse loss was still protected at peak EAE

missed_core_items.description: The study found that synapse loss in the LGN can occur in the absence of significant demyelination, cell death, or axon degeneration at early stages of mouse EAE.

missed_core_items.description: The study used two mouse models: MOG35-55 EAE and Plp1-CreERT;ROSA26-EGFP-DTA (DTA) model of primary demyelination.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: We assessed two distinct mouse models: a model of inflammatory demyelination and a model of primary demyelination. Inflammatory demyelination was induced using the MOG35–55 C57Bl6/J mouse EAE model

missed_core_items.description: The study assessed synapse loss in the somatosensory cortex and found that AAV-Crry did not protect synapses there, indicating circuit specificity.

research_questions.statement: Do complement and microglia mediate synapse loss in demyelinating disease?

provenance.text_excerpt: Synapse-Localized Crry blocks Microglial Synapse Engulfment, Rescues Synapse Loss, and Restores Visual Function in Demyelinating Disease

claims.statement: AAV-mediated expression of Crry at retinogeniculate synapses inhibits C3 localization, reduces microglial engulfment, rescues synapse loss, and preserves visual function in EAE.

experiments_or_tasks: Analyzed mice at onset (day 11) and peak (day 18) of EAE.
Assessed Crry enrichment at presynaptic terminals, C3 colocalization, and microglial engulfment.
Developed AAV9 vector expressing Crry-CR2 fusion protein (AAV-Crry) to inhibit C3 activation at synapses.
Injected AAV-Crry or AAV-EGFP into vitreous of 4-week-old WT mice, induced EAE 28 days later.

methods.name: AAV-mediated gene therapy
methods.protocol_description: AAV9 vectors encoding Crry-CR2-EGFP or EGFP alone were injected intravitreally. EAE was induced 28 days post-injection. Mice were analyzed at onset and peak of clinical symptoms.

study_units.name: AAV-Crry inhibition of C3 at retinogeniculate synapses

results.value_raw_text: Significant reduction in VGluT2+ and VGluT1+ terminals engulfed within microglial lysosomes of AAV-Crry-treated mice compared to AAV-EGFP controls.

provenance.text_excerpt: there was a pronounced decrease in the colocalization of C3 with VGluT2+-retinogeniculate terminals in AAV-Crry-treated EAE mice at the onset of disease compared to AAV-EGFP controls

results.value_raw_text: Pronounced decrease in colocalization of C3 with VGluT2+ retinogeniculate terminals in AAV-Crry-treated EAE mice at onset compared to AAV-EGFP controls.

provenance.text_excerpt: AAV-Crry treatment significantly blocked loss of visual acuity in mice at both the onset and peak of EAE.

results.value_raw_text: AAV-Crry treatment significantly blocked loss of visual acuity in mice at both onset and peak of EAE.

results.value_raw_text: Crry was highly enriched at presynaptic terminals within LGN of AAV-Crry injected mice.

provenance.text_excerpt: Profound synapse loss and engulfment of synaptic material by microglia, but not astrocytes, were detected in the LGN from human MS tissue and in all MS-relevant animal models.

claims.statement: MS patients exhibit profound synapse loss and microglial engulfment of presynaptic terminals in the retinogeniculate system.

experiments_or_tasks: Assessed retinogeniculate presynaptic terminals (VGluT2) in postmortem LGN from MS patients and controls via immunostaining and confocal imaging.
Colabeled with Iba1 and performed 3D surface rendering to quantify engulfment of VGluT2+ terminals within microglia.
Corroborated findings in marmoset EAE model induced by human white matter homogenate immunization.

methods.name: Immunohistochemistry and confocal imaging
methods.protocol_description: Anti-VGluT2 immunostaining for retinogeniculate presynaptic inputs, Iba1 for microglia/macrophages, confocal imaging, and 3D surface rendering.

study_units.name: Human MS and marmoset EAE synapse loss and microglial engulfment

results.value_raw_text: Significant amounts of VGluT2+ terminals were engulfed within Iba1+ cells with morphological characteristics of microglia.

provenance.text_excerpt: we observed a significant decrease in retinogeniculate presynaptic terminals within the LGN of MS patients compared to controls

results.value_raw_text: Significant decrease in VGluT2+ presynaptic terminals in LGN of MS patients compared to controls.

provenance.text_excerpt: our data support the involvement of the alternative complement cascade, which bypasses C1q and works directly through synapse-localized activated C3, to mediate synapse loss.

claims.statement: Synapse loss in demyelinating disease is associated with synapse-localized complement C3, not C1q, suggesting alternative complement cascade involvement.

experiments_or_tasks: Assessed C1q and C3 protein in LGN of mouse and marmoset EAE via immunostaining.
Quantified colocalization of C1q and C3 with presynaptic terminal markers.

methods.name: Immunostaining for complement factors
methods.protocol_description: Immunostaining for C1q and C3 in LGN sections, colocalization analysis with presynaptic terminal markers (VGluT2).
